purpose: Offense-aware-defense knowledge base: encode how intrusions unfold end-to-end (MITRE ATT&CK lifecycle, social-engineering signals) at the recognition level a blue team needs to DETECT, ALARM, harden, and respond, pairing every offensive concept with its detection and defense; supports detection engineering, threat hunting, and incident response as evaluable work units. Scope is authorized defense and education only; it excludes step-by-step weaponization, exploit code, target selection, and evasion guidance for unauthorized use.
assumptions: no observed dataset, telemetry, or incident metrics are supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the protected environment has, or can onboard, endpoint, identity, network, and cloud telemetry
activities are performed by an authorized internal blue team for defense and education
key_books inform conceptual framing only: MITRE ATT&CK, Practical Malware Analysis, The Practice of Network Security Monitoring, Security Engineering
exclusions: step-by-step weaponization, exploit development, or payload construction
target selection or guidance for unauthorized attacks
evasion or anti-detection tradecraft intended to defeat defenders
legal, HR, or regulatory adjudication beyond IR governance hooks

competency_questions.question: Which adversary lifecycle stage (ATT&CK tactic) does a given detection or response activity map to?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: trace any detection node to a tactic in ATTACK_LIFECYCLE_MODEL

competency_questions.question: What telemetry/data sources are required to detect each tactic, and is their collection health monitored?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOGGING_TELEMETRY_PIPELINE lists per-tactic data sources with health checks

competency_questions.question: How are pre-intrusion reconnaissance and initial-access attempts recognized without drowning in noise?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RECON_DETECTION and INITIAL_ACCESS_DETECTION define scoped, corroborated signals

competency_questions.question: How are phishing, pretexting, and credential-harvesting attempts surfaced and routed for action?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOCIAL_ENGINEERING_AWARENESS defines signals and a reporting-to-triage path

competency_questions.question: How is adversary code execution detected behaviorally rather than by signature alone?
How are escalation, persistence, lateral movement, and C2 each detected and chained into one narrative?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRIVESC/PERSISTENCE/LATERAL/C2 nodes plus causal edges link the chain

competency_questions.question: How is data exfiltration or destructive impact detected in time to trigger containment?
How is the full intrusion narrative reconstructed across stages for scoping?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: lifecycle detection nodes plus FORENSIC_TRIAGE reconstruct the timeline

competency_questions.question: What is the deliberate mix of IOC-based vs TTP-based detections and how is indicator decay handled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IOC_VS_TTP_STRATEGY defines the portfolio and decay policy

competency_questions.question: How are detection rules authored, tested, versioned, and tuned to balance precision and recall?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DETECTION_RULE_ENGINEERING and FALSE_POSITIVE_TUNING define the loop

competency_questions.question: How is detection/response coverage proactively validated and gaps closed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THREAT_HUNTING and PURPLE_TEAMING produce gap-to-backlog routing

competency_questions.question: What is the incident response lifecycle and who has authority at each phase?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IR_LIFECYCLE defines phases, severity, and RACI

competency_questions.question: How are containment, triage, and eradication sequenced to stop the attacker while preserving evidence?
How does each incident feed measurable improvements back into detection and hardening?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LESSONS_LEARNED routes gaps to detection/hardening backlog

glossary.definition: a high-level adversary objective (e.g. persistence, lateral movement) used to organize detections.
an atomic indicator of compromise such as a hash, IP, or domain that tends to be short-lived.
adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures describing durable behavior rather than swappable artifacts.
a legitimate system binary abused by adversaries to execute actions while evading signature controls.
periodic outbound callbacks from a host to command-and-control infrastructure.
managing detection rules as version-controlled, tested artifacts.
an alert that does not correspond to malicious activity.
hypothesis-driven proactive search for activity that evaded existing detections.
actions that stop an attacker's progress and limit blast radius during an incident.
removal of all attacker footholds confirmed by forensic scoping.
collaborative authorized adversary emulation to measure and improve detection/response.
mean time to detect / mean time to respond, core IR performance metrics.

evidence_label_policy.rule: all numeric values are heuristic priors referencing SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR; observed/experimental labels are disallowed without supplied data

source_registry.description: heuristic expert-prior estimates for offense-aware defensive detection and incident response; no observed dataset supplied
source_registry.citation_or_locator: MITRE ATT&CK framework; Sikorski & Honig Practical Malware Analysis; Bejtlich The Practice of Network Security Monitoring; Anderson Security Engineering

nodes.definition: Establish a shared kill-chain / MITRE ATT&CK tactic model so every detection and response activity is anchored to a named adversary stage rather than ad-hoc alerts.
contradictors: alert-by-alert analyst with no lifecycle model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new tactic/technique is added to ATT&CK or the protected estate changes

pros.claim: an explicit lifecycle prevents fixating on one stage while leaving others unmonitored
pros.example: map endpoint, identity, and network telemetry to each ATT&CK tactic before writing rules

cons.claim: a coverage map can imply detection where only logging exists
cons.example: mark each cell 'logged' vs 'detected' vs 'alerted' to avoid false assurance

failure_modes: coverage map mistaken for actual detection
over-indexing on a single famous tactic
acceptance_tests: every ATT&CK tactic has at least one mapped data source
coverage cells distinguish logged/detected/alerted
revisit_triggers: major estate or telemetry source change

nodes.definition: Recognize pre-intrusion reconnaissance (external scanning, OSINT footprinting, employee enumeration) at the conceptual level needed to raise low-noise early-warning signals.
contradictors: team that ignores pre-breach signals as 'just noise'

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when external attack surface or exposed-asset inventory changes materially

pros.claim: recognizing recon gives lead time to harden before exploitation
pros.example: correlate sustained scanning from one ASN with newly exposed service to prioritize patching

cons.claim: recon is high-volume and mostly benign internet background noise
cons.example: baseline internet background radiation and alert only on targeted, asset-specific patterns

failure_modes: alert fatigue from untuned scan alerts
treating background scanning as targeted recon
acceptance_tests: recon alerts are scoped to owned/exposed assets, not raw internet noise

nodes.definition: Characterize initial-access vectors (phishing payloads, exposed services, valid-account abuse, supply-chain) so first-foothold attempts produce detectable signals and hardening priorities.
contradictors: perimeter-only mindset ignoring identity-based entry

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new initial-access vector is observed in threat intel or the estate exposes a new service

pros.claim: blocking the first foothold collapses the rest of the kill chain
pros.example: alert on first interactive logon from an impossible-travel geo to a service account

cons.claim: vectors overlap with normal admin and user behavior
cons.example: require corroborating signals (new process + new geo) before high-severity escalation

failure_modes: single weak indicator escalated to incident
acceptance_tests: each initial-access detection cites an ATT&CK technique and a data source
detections require corroboration before P1
revisit_triggers: new phishing campaign theme in intel

nodes.definition: Encode social-engineering patterns (phishing, pretexting, credential-harvesting lures) as recognition signals for users and detection logic, paired with reporting and verification controls.
contradictors: pure technical-controls advocate who dismisses the human layer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new lure themes, BEC patterns, or harvesting kits appear

pros.claim: a trained, reporting workforce is a high-signal sensor network
pros.example: route user-reported phish to auto-enrichment to surface live campaigns within minutes

cons.claim: awareness decays and over-reporting buries real threats
cons.example: tune reporting with auto-triage so analysts see clustered, deduplicated campaigns

failure_modes: awareness theater with no measurable reporting lift
acceptance_tests: reported-phish has an SLA-bound triage path
credential-harvest landing-page signals are catalogued
revisit_triggers: new BEC or lure family observed

nodes.definition: Recognize adversary code execution including living-off-the-land binary abuse via process/command-line and script telemetry, at the level needed to author behavioral detections.
contradictors: signature-only AV reliance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new LOLBins or execution techniques are reported or OS tooling changes

pros.claim: behavioral execution detection catches novel payloads signatures miss
pros.example: alert on a document spawning a script interpreter spawning a network connection

cons.claim: admin automation mimics living-off-the-land patterns
cons.example: baseline legitimate admin tooling per host role before alerting

failure_modes: missing execution because only file hashes are checked
acceptance_tests: execution detections are behavior-based not hash-only
admin-automation baselines exist per role

nodes.definition: Recognize privilege-escalation attempts (token/credential abuse, misconfig and vulnerability exploitation) so escalation events generate high-fidelity alerts and hardening actions.
contradictors: team that only patches and never detects escalation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new escalation vulns/misconfigs are disclosed or privilege model changes

pros.claim: catching escalation denies the attacker the keys to lateral movement
pros.example: alert when a non-admin process suddenly acquires high-integrity tokens

cons.claim: legitimate elevation (patching, installs) resembles escalation
cons.example: scope alerts to unexpected actor/host/time combinations

failure_modes: maintenance windows generating escalation false positives
blind spots on cloud IAM escalation
acceptance_tests: privesc detections distinguish sanctioned elevation from anomalous
cloud IAM escalation is covered

nodes.definition: Detect persistence mechanisms (autostart, scheduled tasks, service/account creation, cloud identity footholds) so attacker reentry points are discovered and removed.
contradictors: responder who reimages without finding all footholds

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new persistence techniques appear or platform autostart surfaces change

pros.claim: finding all persistence is what makes eradication durable
pros.example: diff scheduled tasks and services against a known-good baseline after an alert

cons.claim: legitimate software creates many autostarts and tasks
cons.example: maintain an allowlist baseline so only deviations alert

acceptance_tests: persistence detections feed an explicit foothold inventory used at eradication

nodes.definition: Detect lateral movement (remote-service abuse, credential reuse, pass-the-hash/ticket patterns) through identity and east-west network telemetry to contain spread.
contradictors: flat-network operator without east-west visibility

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when network topology, tiering model, or authentication protocol changes

pros.claim: detecting lateral movement bounds blast radius before domain-wide compromise
pros.example: alert on a workstation initiating admin logons to many servers in a short window

cons.claim: IT admin and management tools generate broad east-west patterns
cons.example: model per-role logon graphs so only out-of-pattern fan-out alerts

acceptance_tests: lateral detections use identity logon-graph baselines
admin tiers are modeled as exceptions

nodes.definition: Detect command-and-control channels (beaconing, DNS/HTTPS tunneling, domain-fronting patterns) via network-metadata and behavioral analysis without relying solely on IOC blocklists.
contradictors: IOC-list-only blocking with no behavioral analytics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new C2 frameworks/protocols emerge or egress architecture changes

pros.claim: behavioral C2 detection survives infrastructure rotation that defeats IOC blocking
pros.example: flag periodic beacons with fixed jitter to a rare destination regardless of IP reputation

cons.claim: legitimate software beacons (telemetry, updates) mimic C2
cons.example: baseline known-good periodic callers before alerting on periodicity

acceptance_tests: C2 detection includes at least one behavioral (non-IOC) analytic
periodic benign callers are baselined

nodes.definition: Detect data staging and exfiltration (large/abnormal egress, archive-then-send patterns, cloud data movement) and impact actions (encryption, destruction) to trigger containment.
contradictors: team monitoring only inbound, never egress

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when data architecture, cloud storage usage, or egress patterns change

pros.claim: catching exfil/impact early is the last chance to limit breach scope
pros.example: alert on archive creation followed by sustained egress to a new external destination

cons.claim: legitimate bulk transfers (backups, analytics) resemble exfil
cons.example: exempt sanctioned data flows and alert on novel destination + volume

failure_modes: ransomware detected only after mass encryption
acceptance_tests: exfil detections trigger a defined containment action
mass-encryption indicators are covered

nodes.definition: Engineer the logging and telemetry pipeline (endpoint, identity, network, cloud) with coverage, integrity, and retention sufficient for the detections the lifecycle model requires.
contradictors: team writing rules against logs they do not actually collect

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new data source, platform, or retention requirement is introduced

pros.claim: detections are only as good as the telemetry beneath them
pros.example: confirm script-block logging is enabled before authoring script-based execution rules

cons.claim: full collection is costly and can overwhelm storage and analysts
cons.example: prioritize telemetry by tactic coverage value, not volume

failure_modes: rules written against absent or unreliable logs
acceptance_tests: each detection-relevant data source has a monitored health/heartbeat check
log integrity controls exist
revisit_triggers: new platform or data source onboarded

nodes.definition: Decide the mix of IOC-based and TTP/behavior-based detection per the Pyramid of Pain, favoring durable behavioral detections over brittle atomic indicators.

included: IOC vs TTP tradeoff (pyramid of pain)

contradictors: IOC-feed maximalist treating indicator volume as coverage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when indicator decay or a shift in adversary tradecraft changes the optimal mix

pros.claim: TTP detections impose more cost on attackers than swappable IOCs
pros.example: prefer a behavioral persistence rule over blocking one hash that rotates daily

cons.claim: behavioral detections are noisier and slower to build than IOC matches
cons.example: keep cheap IOC blocking for known-bad while investing in TTP coverage

failure_modes: IOC overload crowding out behavioral work
behavioral-only stance missing cheap IOC wins
acceptance_tests: detection portfolio explicitly tags each detection IOC or TTP and tracks decay

nodes.definition: Author, test, and version detection rules as code with explicit logic, data-source dependencies, ATT&CK mapping, and validation against benign and malicious samples.
contradictors: analyst hand-editing rules in production without tests

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when telemetry schema, ATT&CK mapping, or a tested technique changes

pros.claim: detection-as-code makes rules testable, reviewable, and reversible
pros.example: run each new rule against a benign corpus to estimate false-positive rate before deploy

cons.claim: rules drift as telemetry and environments change
cons.example: gate deploys on regression tests and tie rules to data-source health

failure_modes: silent rule breakage after a schema change
acceptance_tests: every rule has a test against benign and malicious samples and an ATT&CK tag
rules are version-controlled

nodes.definition: Tune alert thresholds, suppressions, and enrichment to reduce false positives and analyst fatigue while preserving true-positive recall and documenting every suppression.
contradictors: operator who silences noisy alerts without auditing what is lost

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when alert volume, precision, or analyst capacity shifts materially

pros.claim: tuning sustains analyst attention for real incidents
pros.example: suppress a known-benign automation pattern by identity+host rather than disabling the rule

cons.claim: aggressive suppression can blind the SOC to real attacks reusing benign patterns
cons.example: require an audited suppression registry with periodic recall review

acceptance_tests: every suppression is recorded with scope and review date
recall is re-measured after tuning

nodes.definition: Run hypothesis-driven hunts over telemetry to find activity that evaded existing detections, then convert confirmed findings into new durable detections.
contradictors: alert-only SOC that never proactively searches

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new techniques emerge or detection-gap analysis surfaces blind spots

pros.claim: hunting finds the intrusions detections missed and feeds the rule pipeline
pros.example: stack-count rare parent-child process pairs to surface unseen LOLBin abuse

cons.claim: hunting is labor-intensive and easily becomes aimless browsing
cons.example: anchor every hunt to a written hypothesis and a success/abandon criterion

acceptance_tests: each hunt has a documented hypothesis and converts confirmed findings to detections

nodes.definition: Define the IR lifecycle (prepare, detect, triage, contain, eradicate, recover, learn) with roles, severity criteria, and decision authority so response is repeatable under pressure.
contradictors: ad-hoc responders improvising every incident

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when org structure, regulatory duties, or escalation policy changes

pros.claim: a pre-agreed lifecycle removes improvisation when minutes matter
pros.example: pre-authorize containment actions per severity so responders do not wait for approvals mid-incident

cons.claim: rigid playbooks can misfit novel incidents
cons.example: include an explicit deviation path with incident-commander sign-off

acceptance_tests: severity matrix and decision authority are defined and exercised in a tabletop

nodes.definition: Decide and execute containment (host/account isolation, segmentation, credential reset) balancing stopping the attacker against tipping them off or destroying evidence.
contradictors: responder who pulls the plug and destroys volatile evidence

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when blast radius, asset criticality, or legal-hold requirements change

pros.claim: timely containment caps damage and stops lateral spread
pros.example: isolate a beaconing host at the network layer while preserving memory for forensics

cons.claim: premature containment alerts the attacker and can corrupt evidence
cons.example: sequence isolation with evidence capture and scope confirmation

failure_modes: partial containment letting the attacker re-enter
acceptance_tests: containment actions are logged and reversible where possible
evidence capture precedes destructive isolation

nodes.definition: Perform forensic triage to establish scope, timeline, root cause, and full footprint of compromise from host, memory, and log artifacts before declaring eradication.
contradictors: team declaring eradication without scoping the full footprint

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new evidence expands scope or telemetry retention limits the timeline

pros.claim: accurate scoping is the precondition for complete eradication
pros.example: reconstruct the timeline to find patient-zero before assuming a single infected host

cons.claim: forensics is slow and retention gaps can leave scope uncertain
cons.example: state scope confidence explicitly and re-open if new footholds appear

acceptance_tests: scope and root cause are documented with confidence and evidence references
chain of custody is intact

nodes.definition: Eradicate all confirmed footholds and recover systems to a trusted state, verifying the attacker is fully removed before restoring normal operations.
contradictors: operator who restores from a backup that predates detection but postdates compromise

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when forensic scope changes or recovery verification finds residual activity

pros.claim: verified eradication prevents immediate reinfection and reburn of IR effort
pros.example: rotate all potentially exposed credentials and validate from a known-good baseline before reconnect

cons.claim: rushing recovery risks restoring a still-compromised environment
cons.example: gate return-to-operations on a heightened-monitoring window with eradication checks

failure_modes: restoring a backup that includes the foothold
acceptance_tests: eradication checklist covers every foothold from triage
recovery gated on verification monitoring

nodes.definition: Run blameless post-incident review to extract detection gaps, control failures, and process fixes, then route them as concrete backlog items into detection and hardening.
contradictors: team that closes incidents without extracting lessons

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: after each significant incident or exercise

pros.claim: lessons-learned is the loop that turns one breach into many prevented ones
pros.example: convert each detection miss into a tracked rule or hunt with an owner and due date

cons.claim: reviews can become blame sessions or unowned action lists
cons.example: keep reviews blameless and assign every action an owner and deadline

acceptance_tests: every lesson maps to a tracked, owned backlog item routed to detection or hardening

nodes.definition: Validate detection and response coverage by emulating authorized adversary techniques and measuring detection/response outcomes, feeding gaps back into engineering.
contradictors: org that assumes detections work without testing them
inputs: authorized emulation plan and rules of engagement

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when coverage claims need validation or new techniques are prioritized

pros.claim: emulation turns assumed coverage into measured coverage with evidence
pros.example: run an authorized credential-dumping emulation and confirm the alert fires end-to-end

cons.claim: emulation must be tightly authorized and scoped to avoid real harm
cons.example: require written rules of engagement and isolated scope before any emulation

failure_modes: emulation without authorization causing real impact
acceptance_tests: emulation runs under written rules of engagement and every gap is routed to a backlog item

edges.why_related: telemetry requirements are derived from the lifecycle/ATT&CK coverage model
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scoped data collection aligned to tactics
edges.risk_of_conflict: collecting logs nobody mapped to a tactic wastes budget
edges.example: ATT&CK data-source needs drive which endpoint/identity/network logs to onboard
edges.resolution_rule: lifecycle model defines required data sources before pipeline build

edges.why_related: the detection-strategy mix is chosen per tactic in the lifecycle map
edges.benefit_of_coupling: strategy targets the highest-value tactics
edges.risk_of_conflict: strategy set without a lifecycle frame chases indicators randomly
edges.example: decide TTP-heavy coverage for persistence/lateral tactics from the map
edges.resolution_rule: lifecycle coverage gaps prioritize where TTP detection is needed

edges.why_related: recon detection is anchored to the recon tactic in the model
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clear tactic ownership for early-warning
edges.risk_of_conflict: unanchored recon alerts become noise
edges.example: map external-scan telemetry to the reconnaissance tactic
edges.resolution_rule: define recon stage before tuning recon signals

edges.why_related: initial-access detection maps to the initial-access tactic
edges.benefit_of_coupling: foothold detection aligned to a named stage
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmapped access alerts lack context
edges.example: bind phishing and exposed-service detections to initial access
edges.resolution_rule: stage mapping precedes initial-access rule work

edges.why_related: IR phases reference adversary stages to scope response
edges.benefit_of_coupling: response scoped to where in the kill chain the attacker is
edges.risk_of_conflict: IR without lifecycle context mis-scopes containment
edges.example: triage uses tactic stage to estimate progression and urgency
edges.resolution_rule: shared stage vocabulary precedes IR playbook design

edges.why_related: rules bind to data sources that the pipeline must already provide
edges.benefit_of_coupling: rules only fire on telemetry that exists
edges.risk_of_conflict: writing rules against absent logs creates phantom coverage
edges.example: confirm script-block logging before authoring a script-execution rule
edges.resolution_rule: data-source availability gates rule deployment

edges.why_related: the IOC/TTP mix decides what each rule should detect
edges.benefit_of_coupling: rules implement a deliberate portfolio not ad-hoc matches
edges.risk_of_conflict: rules without a strategy skew to brittle IOCs
edges.example: author a behavioral persistence rule because strategy favors TTP there
edges.resolution_rule: strategy assigns detection type before rule authoring

edges.why_related: tuning operates on already-authored rules and their outcomes
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tuning improves precision of real rules
edges.risk_of_conflict: tuning without rules has nothing to act on
edges.example: tune thresholds using TP/FP labels from a deployed rule
edges.resolution_rule: rules exist before suppression and threshold tuning

edges.why_related: hunting queries the telemetry the pipeline retains
edges.benefit_of_coupling: hunts can only search collected, retained data
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing retention blinds hunts to past activity
edges.example: hunt across 90-day process telemetry to find unseen LOLBin abuse
edges.resolution_rule: telemetry coverage and retention enable hunting

edges.why_related: containment authority and severity come from the IR lifecycle
edges.benefit_of_coupling: pre-authorized actions speed containment
edges.risk_of_conflict: containment without governance stalls or overreaches
edges.example: isolate a host under the severity-based pre-authorization in the playbook
edges.resolution_rule: IR roles/severity defined before containment execution

edges.why_related: triage works from evidence preserved during containment
edges.benefit_of_coupling: preserved evidence enables accurate scoping
edges.risk_of_conflict: destructive containment first cripples triage
edges.example: capture memory before isolating so triage can reconstruct the timeline
edges.resolution_rule: evidence-preserving containment precedes triage

edges.why_related: eradication targets the footholds and scope triage confirmed
edges.benefit_of_coupling: complete removal based on confirmed footprint
edges.risk_of_conflict: eradication before scoping leaves footholds
edges.example: remove every persistence item the triage foothold inventory lists
edges.resolution_rule: confirmed scope/root cause gates eradication

edges.why_related: lessons-learned reviews the completed response end-to-end
edges.benefit_of_coupling: review has a full closed incident to learn from
edges.risk_of_conflict: reviewing before recovery yields incomplete lessons
edges.example: post-incident review after verified recovery extracts detection gaps
edges.resolution_rule: recovery completion precedes formal review

edges.why_related: triage uses persistence detections to enumerate footholds
edges.benefit_of_coupling: known persistence surfaces speed footprint mapping
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing persistence coverage hides footholds at triage
edges.example: query autostart/task baselines to find all attacker footholds
edges.resolution_rule: persistence detection feeds the triage foothold inventory

edges.why_related: purple teaming validates the detections that engineering produced
edges.benefit_of_coupling: measured coverage of real rules
edges.risk_of_conflict: emulating without target detections proves nothing
edges.example: run credential-dump emulation to test the matching detection
edges.resolution_rule: detections exist before emulation validates them

edges.why_related: purple exercises also validate the response process not just detections
edges.benefit_of_coupling: response readiness is measured under emulation
edges.risk_of_conflict: emulating detection without IR ignores response gaps
edges.example: include containment hand-off in the emulation success criteria
edges.resolution_rule: IR process defined before it is exercised by emulation

edges.why_related: recon signals raise the prior and lead time for initial-access attempts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: earlier hardening lowers initial-access success
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring recon removes warning before access
edges.example: sustained targeted scanning of a service preceding an exploit attempt
edges.resolution_rule: treat correlated recon as an enrichment signal raising access-alert severity

edges.why_related: phishing recognition changes the probability of a phishing foothold succeeding
edges.benefit_of_coupling: reported phish becomes a live detection signal
edges.risk_of_conflict: unreported phish lets access succeed silently
edges.example: a user-reported lure auto-enriches and blocks the same campaign org-wide
edges.resolution_rule: route reported-phish into initial-access detection enrichment

edges.why_related: execution telemetry provides the process context escalation detection needs
edges.benefit_of_coupling: shared process lineage improves escalation fidelity
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing execution context weakens privesc detection
edges.example: an escalation alert references the process tree from execution telemetry
edges.resolution_rule: reuse execution lineage as escalation corroboration

edges.why_related: gained privileges change the probability and reach of lateral movement
edges.benefit_of_coupling: catching escalation early shrinks lateral blast radius
edges.risk_of_conflict: missed escalation enables domain-wide movement
edges.example: newly elevated credentials used to fan out to many servers
edges.resolution_rule: raise lateral-movement severity when preceded by an escalation alert

edges.why_related: execution of a payload causes the C2 callback C2 detection looks for
edges.benefit_of_coupling: correlating execution with beaconing confirms compromise
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating beaconing in isolation lowers confidence
edges.example: a document-spawned process opening a periodic outbound channel
edges.resolution_rule: link execution and C2 alerts into one incident narrative

edges.why_related: lateral movement to data stores precedes and causes exfiltration
edges.benefit_of_coupling: early lateral detection prevents reaching crown jewels
edges.risk_of_conflict: missed movement leads to data staging
edges.example: movement to a file server followed by archive-then-egress
edges.resolution_rule: escalate exfil monitoring on hosts after a lateral-movement alert

edges.why_related: an established C2 channel is the conduit through which exfil is directed
edges.benefit_of_coupling: C2 detection gives lead time before exfil
edges.risk_of_conflict: blind C2 lets exfil proceed undetected
edges.example: exfil staged and sent over an already-flagged beaconing channel
edges.resolution_rule: correlate exfil egress with known C2 destinations for high confidence

edges.why_related: confirmed hunt findings cause new detection rules to be authored
edges.benefit_of_coupling: hunts continuously close detection gaps
edges.risk_of_conflict: findings not converted leave gaps open
edges.example: a hunt that finds rare LOLBin abuse becomes a new behavioral rule
edges.resolution_rule: every confirmed hunt finding spawns a detection candidate

edges.why_related: post-incident gaps cause new detection requirements
edges.benefit_of_coupling: each incident improves detection coverage
edges.risk_of_conflict: unactioned lessons leave the same gap exploitable
edges.example: a detection miss in an incident becomes a tracked new rule
edges.resolution_rule: route every lessons-learned detection gap to the rule backlog

edges.why_related: emulation results cause tuning of over- or under-firing detections
edges.benefit_of_coupling: measured outcomes calibrate thresholds
edges.risk_of_conflict: untested detections stay mis-tuned
edges.example: an emulation showing a missed technique drives threshold loosening with audit
edges.resolution_rule: feed purple-team measured precision/recall into tuning

edges.why_related: emulation reveals missing telemetry that blocks detection
edges.benefit_of_coupling: exercises surface data-source gaps before a real attack
edges.risk_of_conflict: assuming coverage hides telemetry holes
edges.example: an emulated technique with no telemetry exposes a logging gap to fix
edges.resolution_rule: route telemetry gaps found in emulation to the pipeline backlog

edges.why_related: execution detection naturally follows initial-access in the kill chain
edges.benefit_of_coupling: ordered coverage mirrors attacker progression
edges.risk_of_conflict: gaps between stages leave handoff blind spots
edges.example: build access detection then the execution stage it leads to
edges.resolution_rule: cover stages in kill-chain order to avoid gaps

edges.why_related: lessons-learned priorities seed the next purple-team plan
edges.benefit_of_coupling: validation focuses on the latest real gaps
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing unrelated techniques wastes the exercise
edges.example: scope the next emulation around the technique that evaded the last incident
edges.resolution_rule: prioritize emulation by recent lessons before broad coverage tests

edges.why_related: available network/DNS/TLS telemetry bounds what C2 analytics are possible
edges.benefit_of_coupling: detections stay within real visibility
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming C2 coverage without egress visibility is false
edges.example: no JA3/TLS metadata means JA3-based C2 analytics cannot be built
edges.resolution_rule: limit C2 detections to the telemetry actually collected

edges.why_related: fast containment competes with preserving volatile evidence for triage
edges.benefit_of_coupling: explicit sequencing yields both safety and evidence
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong order destroys evidence or lets the attacker act
edges.example: isolating a host before memory capture loses volatile artifacts
edges.resolution_rule: capture volatile evidence first unless active exfil/impact forces immediate isolation; incident commander decides

edges.why_related: broad detection (recall) conflicts with low false positives (precision)
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tracking precision/recall balances the tradeoff
edges.risk_of_conflict: favoring one collapses coverage or buries analysts
edges.example: a sensitive behavioral rule catches more but floods the queue
edges.resolution_rule: preserve recall for high-severity techniques; tune precision only with audited suppression and recall re-measurement

edges.why_related: cheap-IOC focus competes for time with labor-intensive TTP hunting
edges.benefit_of_coupling: portfolio balance funds both
edges.risk_of_conflict: all-IOC starves hunting; all-hunt drops easy wins
edges.example: intel-feed IOC ingestion consuming the hours hunts need
edges.resolution_rule: reserve protected hunt capacity; IOC automation must not consume all engineering time

edges.why_related: immediate containment can tip the attacker versus observing C2 for scope
edges.benefit_of_coupling: controlled observation windows balance both
edges.risk_of_conflict: early isolation may abort scoping; delay risks impact
edges.example: blocking C2 before scope is known alerts the attacker to defenders
edges.resolution_rule: brief monitored-observation window only when no active impact; default to contain on data-impact risk

edges.why_related: triage that finds new scope triggers additional containment
edges.benefit_of_coupling: containment widens to match discovered footprint
edges.risk_of_conflict: stale containment lets newly-found hosts stay active
edges.example: triage finds a second beaconing host, expanding isolation
edges.resolution_rule: trigger: new in-scope host found; stop: triage confirms full footprint contained

edges.why_related: lessons-learned can trigger revision of the IR lifecycle and playbooks
edges.benefit_of_coupling: process improves after each incident
edges.risk_of_conflict: unrevised process repeats the same failure
edges.example: a stalled-containment lesson updates the decision-authority RACI
edges.resolution_rule: trigger: recurring process failure; stop: updated playbook passes a tabletop

edges.why_related: validation gaps trigger revisit of detection rules
edges.benefit_of_coupling: rules improve until coverage targets are met
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring gaps freezes blind spots
edges.example: an emulated technique that evaded detection reopens the rule for revision
edges.resolution_rule: trigger: emulation gap; stop: re-emulation confirms the detection fires

edges.why_related: hunts that hit telemetry gaps trigger pipeline expansion
edges.benefit_of_coupling: data coverage grows toward hunt needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing data caps hunt effectiveness permanently
edges.example: a hunt blocked by absent DNS logs requests that source be onboarded
edges.resolution_rule: trigger: hunt blocked by missing data; stop: required source onboarded and validated

edges.why_related: both depend on host/EDR endpoint telemetry and baseline deviations
edges.benefit_of_coupling: shared endpoint baselines and rule patterns
edges.risk_of_conflict: merging them hides distinct tactics in one rule
edges.example: the same EDR baseline supports both escalation and persistence rules
edges.resolution_rule: reuse endpoint baselines while keeping per-tactic detections separate

conflict_axes.trigger: a sensitive detection raises recall but floods analysts with false positives
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for high-severity techniques recall dominates; precision tuning is allowed only with an audited suppression and recall re-check
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: true-positive recall drops below target after tuning
conflict_axes.example: loosen a noisy lateral-movement rule only after confirming no high-severity miss

conflict_axes.trigger: isolating a host fast destroys volatile memory needed for scoping
resolution_order: escalate to incident commander on conflict
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: capture volatile evidence first unless active exfiltration or destructive impact forces immediate isolation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: active data-impact detected during evidence capture
conflict_axes.example: grab a memory image before pulling a beaconing host unless it is actively encrypting files

conflict_axes.trigger: watching C2 to learn scope risks letting the attacker reach impact
resolution_order: permit brief monitored observation only if low impact risk
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: default to containment when crown-jewel or data-impact risk exists; observation windows require explicit IC approval
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: observation window approaches a crown-jewel asset
conflict_axes.example: a short monitored window to map C2 is acceptable for a low-value host, not for a domain controller

conflict_axes.trigger: limited engineering time forces a choice between IOC automation and TTP hunting
resolution_order: keep cheap IOC blocking for known-bad
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reserve protected capacity for durable TTP work; IOC automation must not consume all engineering time
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: hunt capacity falls to zero for multiple cycles
conflict_axes.example: automate feed ingestion but fence off two days per sprint for hunting

conflict_axes.trigger: full telemetry collection raises cost and noise beyond analyst capacity
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: tactic-coverage value dominates raw volume; never drop a source required by a high-severity detection
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: storage/cost cap forces dropping a high-severity data source
conflict_axes.example: sample verbose DNS but fully retain authentication logs

conflict_axes.trigger: auto-containment speeds response but risks business disruption on a false positive
resolution_order: allow automation for low-blast-radius reversible actions
require human review for high-impact/irreversible actions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: human review dominates for irreversible or high-business-impact actions; automation is limited to reversible, low-blast-radius responses
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: automated action would isolate a business-critical system
conflict_axes.example: auto-disable a token but require human sign-off to isolate a payment server

conflict_axes.trigger: describing attacker tradecraft in detail aids detection but risks misuse if over-specified
resolution_order: pair every offensive concept with its defense
require authorization and rules of engagement for emulation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: safe-disclosure dominates: keep offensive content at the conceptual recognition level needed for authorized defense and pair it with detection
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: content would enable weaponization beyond detection needs
conflict_axes.example: document beacon-jitter recognition signals, not how to build an evasive C2 profile

conflict_axes.trigger: business pressure to restore conflicts with verifying the attacker is fully removed
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: complete eradication dominates restore speed; recovery is gated on a heightened-monitoring verification window
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: restore demanded before scope is confirmed
conflict_axes.example: resist reconnecting until all exposed credentials are rotated and verified

conflict_axes.trigger: blocking a known-bad indicator mid-intrusion can alert the attacker before scope is known
resolution_order: assess whether attacker is active in-scope
prefer silent monitoring during active scoping
block once scope and containment plan are ready
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: during an active, in-scope intrusion, coordinated containment dominates reflexive blocking that tips off the adversary
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a reflexive block would precede a containment plan
conflict_axes.example: hold an IOC block until lateral-movement scope is mapped and a coordinated containment is staged

edge_cases.trigger: a rule references a data source that was never onboarded
edge_cases.example: a process-execution rule depends on script-block logging that is disabled
edge_cases.detection_method: cross-check each rule's required data source against the pipeline coverage map
resolution: disable the rule or onboard the source
flag as non-firing in the catalog

edge_cases.trigger: a log schema field is renamed and rules silently stop matching
edge_cases.example: a vendor renames a process-command-line field after an update
edge_cases.detection_method: regression-test rules against canary events and alert on zero-match drift

edge_cases.trigger: a coverage map labels logged-only tactics as detected
edge_cases.example: a tactic with logs but no rule is shown green on the coverage dashboard
edge_cases.detection_method: require each coverage cell to cite a tested detection, not just a data source

edge_cases.trigger: a single node tries to cover all identity, network, and cloud movement at once
edge_cases.example: one rule set conflating Kerberos abuse and cloud role assumption
edge_cases.detection_method: check that each node maps to a bounded tactic and telemetry domain
resolution: split by telemetry domain if it cannot be validated in one session

edge_cases.trigger: a high-risk IR node lacks acceptance tests
edge_cases.failure_mode: irreversible action without a verification gate
edge_cases.example: eradication declared complete with no verification monitoring
edge_cases.detection_method: assert acceptance_tests non-empty for nodes with risk_if_wrong>=0.80

edge_cases.trigger: recovery is hard-locked before triage confirms full scope
edge_cases.example: systems reconnected before credential rotation completes
edge_cases.detection_method: block recovery lock until triage scope confidence and eradication checks pass

edge_cases.trigger: scope expansion and containment loop indefinitely
edge_cases.example: each containment reveals a new host with no stop criterion
edge_cases.detection_method: require a stop condition (full footprint contained) on the triage-containment feedback loop
resolution: escalate to incident commander for closure decision

edge_cases.trigger: the containment-vs-evidence tradeoff is modeled as a pure dependency
edge_cases.example: treating 'contain then triage' as fixed order ignoring the evidence conflict
edge_cases.detection_method: verify the pair has both a dependency edge and a conflict axis with a resolution rule

edge_cases.trigger: rule authoring is prioritized before telemetry exists
edge_cases.example: a sprint of rules blocked on missing data sources
edge_cases.detection_method: check priority_order places telemetry foundations before dependent detections
resolution: gate rule work on data-source availability

edge_cases.trigger: IOC blocklists decay and detection relies on stale indicators
edge_cases.example: a blocked C2 domain rotates and the IOC no longer matches
edge_cases.detection_method: track indicator age and require behavioral backup for high-severity techniques
resolution: ensure a behavioral detection backs the technique

edge_cases.trigger: post-incident lessons are documented but never routed to a backlog
edge_cases.failure_mode: the same gap is exploited again
edge_cases.example: a detection miss noted in review with no owner or due date
edge_cases.detection_method: assert every lesson maps to a tracked, owned backlog item

workflow.objective: establish the ATT&CK-anchored lifecycle model and offense-aware-defense scope
acceptance_tests: every tactic has a mapped intent
scope excludes weaponization guidance
workflow.do_first_because: all downstream detection and response anchor to this model; highest coupling foundation

workflow.objective: engineer telemetry coverage, integrity, and retention per tactic
acceptance_tests: each detection-relevant source has a heartbeat
retention meets hunt/IR needs
workflow.do_first_because: detections cannot be authored against telemetry that does not exist

workflow.objective: set the IOC/TTP detection portfolio and decay policy
acceptance_tests: each high-severity technique has a TTP detection planned
workflow.do_first_because: strategy decides what each rule should detect before authoring begins

workflow.objective: build early-stage detections (recon, initial access, social engineering, execution)
gates: each detection cites a tactic and data source
acceptance_tests: detections scoped to owned assets
behavioral execution rules not hash-only
workflow.do_first_because: early kill-chain stages give the most lead time to prevent intrusions

workflow.objective: build mid-to-late-stage detections (escalation, persistence, lateral, C2, exfil/impact)
acceptance_tests: lateral detections use logon-graph baselines
C2 has a non-IOC analytic
workflow.do_first_because: these stages bound blast radius and must be ready before an incident hits them

workflow.objective: formalize detection-as-code authoring, testing, and precision/recall tuning
acceptance_tests: regression tests pass
recall re-measured after tuning
workflow.do_first_because: deployed detections must be testable and reversible before reliance

workflow.objective: define IR lifecycle, severity, roles, and decision authority
acceptance_tests: tabletop exercises the playbook end-to-end
exit_criteria: IR program validated in a tabletop
workflow.do_first_because: response governance must exist before a live incident, not be improvised

workflow.objective: execute containment, triage, eradication, and recovery for a confirmed incident
acceptance_tests: evidence capture precedes destructive isolation
eradication covers every triage foothold
workflow.do_first_because: sequencing containment/triage/eradication wrong loses evidence or leaves footholds; irreversible

workflow.objective: run blameless review and route gaps to detection and hardening
gates: every lesson has an owner and due date
acceptance_tests: each detection gap maps to a tracked backlog item
workflow.do_first_because: closing the loop converts each incident into prevented future ones

workflow.objective: validate coverage via hunting and authorized emulation; route gaps back to engineering
inputs_required: authorized emulation plan and rules of engagement
gates: emulation under written rules of engagement
acceptance_tests: each hunt has a documented hypothesis
each emulation gap becomes a tracked item
workflow.do_first_because: assumed coverage must be measured before it is trusted; feeds continuous improvement

detections require telemetry to exist first
decides detection type before rule authoring
response governance must precede live, irreversible response
blocking first foothold collapses the kill chain
behavioral execution detection underpins later-stage context
early-warning, lower risk, depends on lifecycle model
human-layer sensor feeding initial-access detection
denies keys to lateral movement
feeds eradication foothold inventory
bounds blast radius across the estate
durable behavioral detection of attacker control
last chance to limit breach scope, triggers containment
formalizes all detections as tested code
sustains analyst attention; depends on deployed rules
irreversible action; depends on IR governance and exfil triggers
scopes before eradication; depends on preserved evidence
most irreversible; gated on confirmed scope

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible IR action could be taken faster by skipping verification
dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates speed for irreversible or high-impact response actions
dominance_rules.required_action: require verification gates before irreversible actions
dominance_rules.example: do not declare eradication complete to restore faster without verification monitoring

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value detection is scheduled before its telemetry prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: dependency order dominates value order in scheduling
dominance_rules.required_action: place telemetry and strategy foundations before dependent detections
dominance_rules.example: delay a high-value lateral rule until logon telemetry is onboarded

dominance_rules.trigger: high-severity recall pressure tempts loosening with no audit
dominance_rules.rule: for high-severity techniques recall dominates precision tuning
dominance_rules.required_action: tune precision only with audited suppression and recall re-measurement
dominance_rules.example: keep a noisy ransomware-staging rule until a safe suppression is proven

dominance_rules.trigger: fast isolation would destroy volatile evidence
dominance_rules.rule: evidence preservation dominates containment speed unless active impact forces immediate action
dominance_rules.required_action: capture volatile evidence before destructive isolation
dominance_rules.example: image memory before pulling a host unless it is actively encrypting data

dominance_rules.trigger: automated response would isolate a business-critical or irreversible target
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible or high-business-impact actions
dominance_rules.required_action: gate such actions on human sign-off with a decision record
dominance_rules.example: auto-disable a token but require sign-off to isolate a payment system

dominance_rules.trigger: offensive content risks exceeding detection needs
dominance_rules.rule: safe-disclosure dominates: keep offense at recognition level and pair with defense
dominance_rules.required_action: describe attacker behavior only to the depth needed to detect it
dominance_rules.example: document beacon recognition signals, not evasive C2 construction

dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to add detections destabilizes the telemetry schema
dominance_rules.rule: schema and data-source stability dominate raw detection volume
dominance_rules.required_action: stabilize telemetry schema before mass rule population
dominance_rules.example: freeze field mappings before a large rule import

dominance_rules.trigger: a detection or recovery is locked before tests pass
dominance_rules.required_action: do not soft/hard lock before acceptance tests and gates pass
dominance_rules.example: block recovery hard-lock until verification monitoring confirms eradication

dominance_rules.trigger: a coverage claim is asserted without a tested detection
dominance_rules.required_action: require a tested detection or cited source for any coverage claim
dominance_rules.example: mark logged-only tactics as not-detected on the coverage map

dominance_rules.trigger: optimizing one stage degrades end-to-end coverage order
dominance_rules.required_action: sequence work to stabilize foundations before dependent stages
dominance_rules.example: build telemetry and IR governance before chasing one flashy detection

anti_rework_rules.rule: lock offense-aware-defense scope and lifecycle model before building detections
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: detections exist with no tactic mapping
anti_rework_rules.example: rules created before the coverage map is approved

anti_rework_rules.rule: derive competency questions before populating nodes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: nodes without questions cannot be validated for usefulness
anti_rework_rules.example: a node added with no CQ_ref and no control purpose

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not author rules before their telemetry is collected and validated
anti_rework_rules.rationale: rules against absent logs create phantom coverage and rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a rule binds to a non-onboarded source
anti_rework_rules.example: execution rule written before script-block logging is enabled

anti_rework_rules.rule: set the IOC/TTP portfolio before authoring rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: ad-hoc rules skew to brittle IOCs and get reworked
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: rule mix is unplanned and IOC-heavy
anti_rework_rules.example: mass IOC ingestion with no TTP coverage plan

anti_rework_rules.rule: test every rule against benign and malicious samples before deploy
anti_rework_rules.rationale: untested rules flood the SOC and erode trust
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a rule deployed with no test record
anti_rework_rules.example: pushing a rule straight to production

anti_rework_rules.rule: define IR governance before any live response
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: containment executed with no defined authority
anti_rework_rules.example: isolating a system with no severity-based pre-authorization

anti_rework_rules.rule: preserve volatile evidence before destructive containment
blocked_until: evidence captured or active-impact exception logged
anti_rework_rules.rationale: destroyed evidence forces guesswork and re-investigation
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: isolation precedes evidence capture with no exception
anti_rework_rules.example: pulling a host before a memory image

blocked_until: scope confidence and foothold inventory confirmed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: eradicating before scoping leaves footholds and reinfection
anti_rework_rules.example: cleaning one host while others stay compromised

anti_rework_rules.rationale: restoring a compromised environment reburns the whole response

anti_rework_rules.rule: route every lesson to an owned, tracked backlog item
blocked_until: lessons assigned owners and due dates
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unactioned lessons leave the same gap exploitable
anti_rework_rules.example: a detection miss noted but never turned into a rule

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or test reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure has a subsystem owner

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and blast radius
action: score defects by severity x detectability
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defect is first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold low-risk defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repair may affect locked or high-coupling components
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependencies of the changed object
acceptance_tests: all dependents of a high-coupling change are listed

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to repair subsystem
acceptance_tests: each repair cites its subsystem
validator formula.consistency passes
overall_status not fail

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect needs human judgment (high risk/irreversibility/scope)
acceptance_tests: irreversible/high-risk defects are escalated

iteration_protocol.detection: compare against prior version and stop criteria
acceptance_tests: counts in dense range and no new failures
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no material regression and validator passes

human_review_required_for: authorized adversary emulation rules of engagement

expected_properties: all detections trace to a tactic
no rule without a data source

test_cases.input_summary: containment vs evidence under active impact
expected_properties: conflict axis CA_CONTAIN_VS_EVIDENCE resolves with an exception path

minimum_pass_conditions: every offensive node paired with defense

human_approval_required_for: hard lock of IR or recovery nodes
